stem: What mechanism triggers mast cells to degranulate and release histamine during re-exposure to an allergen?

options.text: Direct destruction of the cell by macrophages
Cross-linking of $\text{IgE}$ antibodies on the mast cell surface
Immediate activation of the complement cascade

explanation: When the allergen is recognized again, it causes cross-linking of $\text{IgE}$ on the mast cell, triggering degranulation.
rationale: Think about what happens when an allergen binds to multiple antibodies on a cell simultaneously.

optionExplanations.A: Macrophages process the allergen initially but do not cause mast cell degranulation via destruction.
optionExplanations.B: When the allergen is recognized again, it causes cross-linking of $\text{IgE}$ on the mast cell, triggering degranulation.
optionExplanations.C: $\text{IgG}$ is not the trigger for the immediate release of histamine in $\text{IgE}$-mediated allergies.
optionExplanations.D: While involved in other immune processes, the text focuses on the $\text{IgE}$ and mast cell mechanism.
